name: commons-draw-three
description: ⭐ THE ORCHARD BOARD AT DRAW 3, AND IT IS THE ONE CONTESTED DOOR NUMBER IN THE COMMONS. Dean chose Draw 2 on 09/09/2026 (C3: "Dean chose 2 over 3; Draw 3 is a paired arm"), so this arm is that paired arm and it is the falsifier for his choice. THE ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS HALF THE OLD ONE. A commons play costs ONE CARD from your hand, and the fee is extra in every case. So the Wheat board buys a Harvest, the Dairy board a whole Build, the Apiary board a Grow, the Vegetable board a Deliver - each a complete core action for one card - while the Orchard board at Draw 2 returns two cards for one, netting +1. That is the thinnest return in the set by a distance, and it is thin for a reason that survives from v31: an action priced in its own output currency has to over-deliver or buying it is nearly pointless. ⚠️ WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE is the other half of the old law. Under v31 the yardstick was a FREE Draw 1 sitting in the same slot, so Draw 2 was strictly worse than doing nothing; the commons has no free option at all (C9), so a Draw 2 board is worth +1 rather than worth nothing, and it may simply be the weakest of five rather than dead. THE PREDICTION IS THEREFORE SHARP: under the shipped Draw 2 the Orchard board should take the LOWEST share of the door mix, and under this arm it should climb toward the other four without passing them. READ IN THIS ORDER. (1) The door mix by board - the whole point - and note that the Orchard board should not need to WIN the mix for 3 to be the right number, only to stop being dead. (2) The bonus rate against Dean's 30-60% band, because a better Orchard board raises the rate at every seat and could push it out of the band on its own. (3) Cards drawn per turn and the median hand, which is the sanity check that the arm did what it says, and the warning that a Draw 3 board feeds a hand limit that is the simulator's bound rather than a rule (C7). (4) The barn glut, because the fastest route from a card to a barn is now a central Harvest and this arm puts more cards in more hands. ⛔ THE OTHER DIAL IS NOT THIS NUMBER. If the Orchard board is dead at 2 and overpowered at 3, the answer may be that a draw board does not belong in a set where every other board sells an action, which is a design question and not a knob. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
